slides.title: The Weisfeiler-Lehman (WL) Test
text: The graph isomorphism problem is NP intermediate
• Not known to be solvable in polynomial time, nor to be NP complete.
The WL test is a combinatorial heuristic to test graph isomorphism.
• If two graphs are distinguished by the WL test, they are non-isomorphic.
• If two graphs are non-distinguishable by the WL test, no conclusion.
Expressive power of GNNs are mainly expressed by the WL test hierarchy.

slides.title: Graph Substructure Networks (GSNs)
text: GSNs are strictly more powerful than MPNNs when:
• ℋ contains substructures other than stars;
• ℋ contains any substructures with ≥ 3 nodes matched via induced isomorphisms.
GSNs are not less powerful than 3-WL even with fixed size substructures.
GSNs can be made universal at high preprocessing cost.

slides.title: Are Subgraph GNNs the Ultimate Answer?
text: Are Subgraph GNNs the Ultimate Answer?
A great candidate for more expressive GNNs:
• Can be tractable (e.g., with node-based policies)
• Complexity is prohibitive in large graphs
• Upper bounds can be tuned with 𝑘, but at the cost
of an exponential in 𝑘 running time.
